newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina to finance pension debt with bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Argentina to finance pension debt with bond issue.

text.p: Argentina will finance backdated payments to pensioners from August 1992 to December 1994 by issuing bonds, said the Economy Ministry's Coordation Secretary Julio Caceres Monday.
He told a news conference that the other part of the pension payments the government now has to make, from April 1991 to August 1992, will be paid with Bocon Previsional bond series one and two.
However, the government did not specify whether it already has the bonds in its portfolio or whether it will buy them in the market.
The decision comes after Argentina's Supreme Court ruled Friday in a case brought by 70,000 pensioners that state pension payments from 1991 to 1994 will be adjusted upwards by 13.8 percent.

The ruling reestablished the mobility of pensions in line with increases in the cost of living. The government's Convertibility Plan introduced in 1991, pegging the value of the peso to the dollar at par, had fixed pension payments.
There is still no official word on the size or timing of the pension payments, but private estimates put the figure at no more than $700 million.
Caceres said at the moment "it is impossible to estimate" the amount the government will have to pay.
The government will need prior approval from Congress to issue bonds to cover the payment.
